feature: A component holds more than one version of itself
summary: One component can now carry its normal look and its disabled look under one name, and every copy picks which one it shows from a Version menu. Before this you made a second component and the two drifted apart the first time you edited one.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Flags are on by default (next-components). Open a blank canvas and show the Library on the Comps shelf.

try.do: Drag the Button tile from the Library onto the canvas, then click it.
In the Component section, press Add beside Versions, and type Disabled over the name that lands selected.
With that new drawing still selected, drag the Effects section's Opacity slider down to about a third.
Drag the Button tile out twice more to place two copies below.
Click one copy and set the Version row at the top of its knobs to Disabled.
Click the Default drawing and change the wording of its label, and watch which copies follow.
Select the Disabled drawing and press Command Delete.

evaluate: Does Add beside Versions read as making another look of this same button, rather than making a second component?
The new drawing lands loose on the canvas to the right of the one it came from. Is that where you expected to find it?
On a copy, the Version row sits above the knobs but four sections down the dock, so you scroll to reach it. Is that far enough down to be annoying?
When you deleted the version a copy was showing, did 'Version deleted, 1 copy moved to Default' tell you enough to decide whether to undo?
Two drawings on the canvas both say Button. Is the version name in the layers list enough to tell them apart, or does the canvas need to say it too?
rough: A change meant for every version has to be made in each one. That was the cost you accepted with the decision on 2026-09-05; a task is filed for making one edit reach them all.
The canvas label above each drawing says only the component name, so the two versions look identical from the picture alone. Filed as a follow-up.
Dropping a component from the shelf always places the first version; picking the version at the shelf is filed as a follow-up.

In a narrow dock the layers row gives the layer name away before the version chip, so a row can read 'B...' beside 'Default'. The chip is the word that tells two rows apart, so it keeps its width on purpose.
The screenshots here are real captures of the app taken by a scripted walk (Scripts/playtest/component-versions-walk.json), not offscreen renders.
